result:
The old bookstore on Maple Street has always been my sanctuary. It’s one of those places where the air smells like yellowed paper and old coffee, where the shelves groan under the weight of forgotten stories. I’d spend hours there as a kid, running my fingers along the spines of books I couldn’t afford, dreaming of the worlds inside. Now, as an adult, I still find myself lingering in the musty corners, flipping through pages that whisper secrets to me.

Lately, I’ve been thinking about how much of life is just waiting—waiting for the right moment, the right person, the right book to fall into your hands. There’s a quiet magic in that pause, that suspended animation between one chapter and the next. Maybe that’s why I love books so much: they teach you to savor the in-between. A story doesn’t rush you. It lets you linger on a single sentence, a character’s hesitation, the way light filters through a window.

I’ve been trying to apply that to my own life. Not everything needs to happen at once. Some days, the most revolutionary thing you can do is sit still. Breathe. Let the world unfold around you without demanding answers. It’s terrifying, really—this idea that you might not have a plan, that you’re just… existing. But there’s a kind of freedom in that too. Like the first time you realize you don’t need to be anywhere important. You can just be.

The bookstore’s owner, Mr. Calloway, once told me that some stories are meant to be read slowly, like a cup of tea on a rainy afternoon. Others are meant to be devoured in one sitting, like a wildfire. Both are necessary. Maybe life is the same. Some moments are for savoring; others are for burning bright and fast. And that’s okay.

I don’t know where I’m going next. But for now, I’m happy right here, between the pages.
